Usage: demux [options]

Route each line of stdin to files or commands by regex; unmatched lines pass through to stdout.

Options:
  --all                        Broadcast: route to every matching route (default: first-match)
  --append                     File targets append instead of truncate
  --exit-on-child-error        A watched child's non-zero exit makes demux exit 2
  --field N                    Test the regex against column N (1-based) instead of the whole line
  --delimiter CHAR             Field delimiter (default: runs of whitespace)
  -h, --help                   Show help
  --version                    Show version
  --no-color                   Disable colored output
  --json                       JSON output
  --describe                   Structured JSON metadata for AI agents
  --color[=auto|always|never]  Coloured output: auto (default when omitted), always, or never

Routes:
  --to PATTERN FILE     Route lines matching regex PATTERN to FILE (repeatable).
  --exec PATTERN CMD    Route matching lines to a command's stdin (shell-spawned, repeatable).
  --default-to FILE     Unmatched records -> FILE.
  --default-exec CMD    Unmatched records -> a command. (Omit both -> unmatched -> stdout.)
  PATTERN is a bare .NET regex (not slash-delimited). Quote it to protect the shell.

Examples:
  cat app.log | demux --to ERROR err.log --default-exec 'gzip > rest.gz'  Split errors into a file, compress the rest

Composes with:
  demux --exec ERROR clip --default-to rest.log  Copy error lines to the clipboard, file the rest

Exit Codes:
  0    Success — all input routed and delivered
  1    Partial delivery failure — a route died, records undelivered
  2    Watched child exited non-zero (--exit-on-child-error)
  125  Usage error
  126  Setup failure — could not open a --to file or launch the shell
